messages:
Anna: quick brain-dump — thinking about a "header-first" fast path for loading shards when we don't have a manifest. goal: let serving start speculative warmup with only minimal metadata validated.
Mike: explain header-first a bit? how minimal is minimal? :thinking:
Anna: read-only header (magic, version, per-chunk offsets + sizes, optional fast-checksum). not the full index. idea is we can mmap/stream header, kick off KV-cache warmup for the most-hot chunks while the heavyweight verify runs async.
Leo: worried about safety — if header is corrupted we might warmup wrong offsets and OOM or corrupt GPU memory mapping.
Anna: yep. mitigation: small bloom/presence vector in the header and a lightweight header-signature check. if bloom says chunk absent, don't speculatively map it. full checksum still runs before final activation.
Sarah: can we make the bloom optional per-bundle? some bundles will be generated by 3rd-party tools that don't produce bloom. fallback?
Priya: fallback should be index-first warmup if header metadata insufficient. but we should prioritize fast path for our verified bundles -> small flag in header: "fast-ready:1".
Mike: serializers will need to emit that bit. Also need a way to advertise safety level: e.g., fast-ready, signed-header, or strict-indexed.
Anna: agreed. sketch of loader API surface: 
```
openShard(path, headerOnly=true) -> HeaderHandle
HeaderHandle.speculativeWarmup(hotRanges, options={prefetchBudget: 20})
HeaderHandle.commit() // waits for verify and flips to full active mapping
```
Mike: nice. where does backpressure live? if many shards call speculativeWarmup simultaneously we need a cluster-level budget.
Tom: infra-bot: alloc-bucket check: we already expose node-level prefetch tokens. should we extend to per-tenant warmup buckets?
infra-bot: suggested: use existing token-bucket with warmup_priority tag. throttle when tokens <= 0, queue by priority.
Leo: also bring up partial gzip/concatenated shard support — header-first can't read offsets if gzip blocks change sizes.
Anna: for compressed shards, header will contain compressed-chunk-entries (compressed_size, uncompressed_size, compressed_offset). loader can still do header-first but prefetch must request compressed ranges and decompress when warming.
Sarah: operationally, how do we handle rolling upgrades of writer tools? older writers won't have bloom/signature. so stepwise rollout: (1) support header-first for fast-ready bundles only; (2) telemetry to count how many bundles are eligible; (3) recommend conversion tool to users.
Priya: important: make sure this doesn't break migration: Dedicated clusters might keep older bundles. we need a safe default: header-first disabled unless bundle explicitly marks fast-ready or service config allows unsafe-fast.
Mike: want a simple on-disk probe: read 4KB header, verify magic, version. If version >= 3 enable bloom & speculative. that keeps cost low.
Anna: also UX: loader should emit traces like `warmup.path=speculative header` and `warmup.result=commit|abort` so Optimize can correlate quality regressions when spec warmup mispredicts.
Leo: edge case: what if the header lies about chunk sizes (attacker or bug)? full checksum may detect it after we've touched GPU memory. we must ensure speculative warmup maps into staging buffers not directly into the inference KV cache until commit.
Anna: yup — staging area in host pinned memory. only after commit we move into device-backed KV cache. commit is atomic from the serving runtime's POV.
Tom: perf question — does staging add too much copy overhead?
Anna: measurable, but for hot chunks most will commit quickly so copy cost amortizes. we can optimize with zero-copy splices when backing store supports it.
Sarah: logging: add a debug trace `header.sig=OK|MISSING|BAD` and `bloom.positive=NNN` so we can aggregate false positive rates.
Mike: rollout plan: implement loader changes + header schema v3, writer sdk bump, console flag to opt-in to speculative warmup per-namespace, and a 30-day telemetry window.
Priya: SLA concerns: we need a circuit-breaker — if speculative warmup causes >X errors in 1h, auto-disable for that cluster.
Anna: +1. I'll draft an RFC addendum with header schema, loader API proto, and a short migration checklist. tagging follow-ups: @Mike for API proto, @Priya for rollout SLOs, @Leo for compression path, @Tom for infra quotas.
Mike: will mock the proto today.
Leo: i'll prototype compressed-chunk warmup (gzip & zstd).
Sarah: I'll add traces and dashboard panels (false-positive rate, warmup-commit latency).
Priya: I'll write the SLA/circuit breaker proposal.
Tom: I'll wire the token-bucket extension to allow warmup_priority tagging.
infra-bot: scheduled reminder: ops-checkpoint in 3 days to review RFC addendum. :calendar:
Anna: thanks all. keeping this header-first path opt-in/observable should keep us safe while giving big warmup wins for verified bundles. :rocket:
